name: Nuclear masses fix the outer-crust composition
summary: The outer-crust sequence of nuclei (56Fe, 62Ni, ..., 78Ni, 82Zn and beyond toward the drip line) follows from measured and extrapolated masses of neutron-rich nuclei; Penning-trap mass measurements at radioactive-beam facilities move the predicted layers.
breaks: The deeper outer crust needs masses beyond experimental reach, so model mass tables take over.
sources: Chamel & Haensel (2008). "Physics of Neutron Star Crusts". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 11, 10. [arXiv:0812.3955](https://arxiv.org/abs/0812.3955)

name: Nuclear structure factors for WIMP-nucleus scattering
summary: Spin-independent and spin-dependent dark-matter rates need nuclear form factors and structure functions computed with the shell model and chiral-EFT currents; the nonrelativistic EFT of direct detection maps each operator onto distinct nuclear responses.
breaks: Two-body currents and nuclear-structure uncertainties grow at large momentum transfer and for odd-unpaired nuclei.
sources: Fitzpatrick et al. (2013). "The Effective Field Theory of Dark Matter Direct Detection". *J. Cosmol. Astropart. Phys.* 02, 004. [arXiv:1203.3542](https://arxiv.org/abs/1203.3542)

Klos et al. (2013). "Large-scale nuclear structure calculations for spin-dependent WIMP scattering with chiral effective field theory currents". *Phys. Rev. D* 88, 083516. [arXiv:1304.7684](https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.7684)

name: Giant-dipole photodisintegration of UHE cosmic-ray nuclei
summary: Ultra-high-energy nuclei are destroyed by photodisintegration when CMB and infrared photons, boosted into the nucleus frame, hit the giant dipole resonance; this shapes the composition and cutoff of the UHECR spectrum alongside the GZK pion threshold for protons.
breaks: Photonuclear cross sections for unstable intermediate nuclei are model-based, and source composition is degenerate with propagation.
sources: Puget, Stecker & Bredekamp (1976). "Photonuclear interactions of ultrahigh energy cosmic rays and their astrophysical consequences". *Astrophys. J.* 205, 638. [doi:10.1086/154321](https://doi.org/10.1086/154321)

name: Band theory of neutrons in the neutron-star crust
summary: Bragg scattering of unbound superfluid neutrons by the nuclear lattice of the inner crust is computed with Bloch's theorem and band-structure methods; the resulting large neutron effective mass (entrainment) reduces the mobile superfluid fraction and challenges crust-only glitch models.
map: \psi_{nk}(\mathbf r+\mathbf R)=e^{i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf R}\psi_{nk}(\mathbf r):\ \text{electrons}\to\text{free neutrons};\ m_n^*/m_n\gg1\ (\text{entrainment})
sources: Chamel (2013). "Crustal Entrainment and Pulsar Glitches". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 110, 011101. [arXiv:1210.8177](https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.8177)
Chamel & Haensel (2008). "Physics of Neutron Star Crusts". *Living Rev. Relativ.* 11, 10. [arXiv:0812.3955](https://arxiv.org/abs/0812.3955)

name: Degenerate Fermi gas: metals and white dwarfs
summary: The same degenerate Fermi-Dirac electron gas gives the Sommerfeld model of metals and the pressure that supports white dwarfs; Fowler applied Fermi statistics to white dwarfs in 1926, before Sommerfeld applied it to metals, and relativistic kinematics turns P~n^{5/3} into P~n^{4/3}, giving the Chandrasekhar mass.
sources: Fowler (1926). "On Dense Matter". *Mon. Not. R. Astron. Soc.* 87, 114. [doi:10.1093/mnras/87.2.114](https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/87.2.114)
Chandrasekhar (1931). "The Maximum Mass of Ideal White Dwarfs". *Astrophys. J.* 74, 81. [doi:10.1086/143324](https://doi.org/10.1086/143324)

name: Superionic water ice in ice-giant interiors
summary: Superionic water, an oxygen crystal through which protons diffuse like a liquid, was predicted by ab initio simulation for Uranus and Neptune and identified in laser-shock experiments by nanosecond X-ray diffraction (fcc ice XVIII); it may explain the ice giants' non-dipolar magnetic fields.
sources: Cavazzoni et al. (1999). "Superionic and Metallic States of Water and Ammonia at Giant Planet Conditions". *Science* 283, 44. [doi:10.1126/science.283.5398.44](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.283.5398.44)
Millot et al. (2019). "Nanosecond X-ray diffraction of shock-compressed superionic water ice". *Nature* 569, 251. [doi:10.1038/s41586-019-1114-6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-019-1114-6)

name: Coulomb crystallization of white-dwarf cores
summary: Carbon-oxygen ions in a cooling white dwarf freeze into a bcc Coulomb (one-component-plasma) crystal near Gamma~175; Gaia's cooling-sequence pile-up confirmed latent-heat release and phase separation, and the same bcc Coulomb lattice makes up neutron-star crusts.
sources: Van Horn (1968). "Crystallization of White Dwarfs". *Astrophys. J.* 151, 227. [doi:10.1086/149432](https://doi.org/10.1086/149432)

Tremblay et al. (2019). "Core crystallization and pile-up in the cooling sequence of evolving white dwarfs". *Nature* 565, 202. [doi:10.1038/s41586-018-0791-x](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-018-0791-x)

name: DFT and dielectric response for dark-matter scattering
summary: Dark-matter-electron scattering rates in crystals are computed from DFT crystal form factors and, with screening included, from the energy-loss function Im[-1/eps(q,omega)], so electronic-structure codes directly set direct-detection sensitivities.
sources: Essig et al. (2016). "Direct Detection of sub-GeV Dark Matter with Semiconductor Targets". *J. High Energy Phys.* 05, 046. [arXiv:1509.01598](https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.01598)
Knapen, Kozaczuk & Lin (2021). "Dark matter-electron scattering in dielectrics". *Phys. Rev. D* 104, 015031. [arXiv:2101.08275](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.08275)

name: Ab initio equations of state for giant-planet interiors
summary: DFT-based molecular dynamics provides the hydrogen-helium equation of state and the H-He immiscibility ('helium rain') used in Jupiter and Saturn interior models fitted to Juno and Cassini gravity data; DFT exchange-correlation and band-gap errors directly shift the predicted metallization boundary.
sources: Morales et al. (2009). "Phase separation in hydrogen-helium mixtures at Mbar pressures". *Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci.* 106, 1324. [doi:10.1073/pnas.0812581106](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.0812581106)

name: Electron transport in white-dwarf and neutron-star matter
summary: Thermal and electrical conductivities of degenerate stellar matter are computed with the Boltzmann/Ziman theory of metals (electron-phonon Umklapp and electron-impurity scattering, Wiedemann-Franz); crust-cooling curves of accreting neutron stars imply a low-impurity, ordered rather than amorphous crust.
sources: Potekhin et al. (1999). "Transport properties of degenerate electrons in neutron star envelopes and white dwarf cores". *Astron. Astrophys.* 346, 345. [arXiv:astro-ph/9903127](https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/9903127)
Brown & Cumming (2009). "Mapping Crustal Heating with the Cooling Light Curves of Quasi-Persistent Transients". *Astrophys. J.* 698, 1020. [arXiv:0901.3115](https://arxiv.org/abs/0901.3115)

name: Single-phonon excitations for sub-MeV dark matter
summary: Below ~MeV the dark matter's momentum transfer is below the inverse lattice spacing, so it scatters by creating single acoustic or optical phonons rather than nuclear recoils; polar crystals (GaAs, sapphire) with dark-photon-coupled optical phonons are proposed targets read out by phonon sensors.
sources: Knapen et al. (2018). "Detection of Light Dark Matter With Optical Phonons in Polar Materials". *Phys. Lett. B* 785, 386. [arXiv:1712.06598](https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.06598)

name: Crustal shear modes as magnetar QPOs
summary: Quasi-periodic oscillations in magnetar giant-flare tails (tens of Hz) are interpreted as global torsional modes of the crystalline crust, i.e. long-wavelength transverse acoustic phonons of the Coulomb lattice whose speed is set by the shear modulus mu~0.12 n_i Z^2 e^2/a.
sources: Strohmayer & Watts (2005). "Discovery of Fast X-Ray Oscillations during the 1998 Giant Flare from SGR 1900+14". *Astrophys. J.* 632, L111. [arXiv:astro-ph/0508206](https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0508206)

name: Debye cooling of crystallized white dwarfs
summary: Once a white-dwarf core crystallizes, its ionic heat capacity follows the Debye phonon law and falls as T^3 below Theta_D, so the oldest white dwarfs cool faster ('Debye cooling'), which shapes the faint end of the luminosity function used for cosmochronology.
sources: Tremblay et al. (2019). "Core crystallization and pile-up in the cooling sequence of evolving white dwarfs". *Nature* 565, 202. [doi:10.1038/s41586-018-0791-x](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-018-0791-x)

name: Semiconductor targets for dark-matter electron recoils
summary: Silicon and germanium crystals are dark-matter targets: ionization-plus-phonon detectors for nuclear recoils, and single-electron skipper CCDs (SENSEI, DAMIC-M) whose ~1 eV band gap lets sub-GeV dark matter register through electron excitations across the gap.
sources: Essig, Mardon & Volansky (2012). "Direct Detection of Sub-GeV Dark Matter". *Phys. Rev. D* 85, 076007. [arXiv:1108.5383](https://arxiv.org/abs/1108.5383)

SENSEI Collaboration (2025). "First Direct-Detection Results on Sub-GeV Dark Matter Using the SENSEI Detector at SNOLAB". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 134, 011804. [arXiv:2312.13342](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.13342)

name: Fullerenes and PAHs: carbon nanostructures in space
summary: C60 was discovered in laser-vaporization experiments built to mimic carbon-star chemistry, opening the fullerene-nanotube-graphene family of carbon materials; fullerenes were later found in planetary nebulae and C60+ identified as a diffuse-interstellar-band carrier.
sources: Kroto et al. (1985). "C60: Buckminsterfullerene". *Nature* 318, 162. [doi:10.1038/318162a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/318162a0)
Cami et al. (2010). "Detection of C60 and C70 in a Young Planetary Nebula". *Science* 329, 1180. [doi:10.1126/science.1192035](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1192035)
Campbell et al. (2015). "Laboratory confirmation of C60+ as the carrier of two diffuse interstellar bands". *Nature* 523, 322. [doi:10.1038/nature14566](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature14566)

name: Wigner crystals and stellar Coulomb crystals
summary: Electron Wigner crystals in moire TMD superlattices and the ion crystals of white dwarfs and neutron-star crusts are both one-component plasmas that crystallize in a uniform neutralizing background once Coulomb energy beats kinetic energy (large r_s or large Gamma).
breaks: Stellar ions melt classically through thermal fluctuations, while 2D electron Wigner crystals melt quantum mechanically; moire Wigner crystals are pinned to an imposed superlattice and are two-dimensional.
sources: Regan et al. (2020). "Mott and generalized Wigner crystal states in WSe2/WS2 moiré superlattices". *Nature* 579, 359. [arXiv:1910.09047](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.09047)

name: Emergent monopoles in spin ice and the monopole problem
summary: Spin-ice excitations behave as deconfined magnetic monopoles with a Coulomb interaction, a condensed-matter realization of the monopoles whose predicted overproduction at grand-unified transitions motivated inflation.
breaks: Spin-ice monopoles source the H field (div M), not B; they are emergent quasiparticles with non-quantized, material-set charge, unlike 't Hooft-Polyakov monopoles of a broken gauge group.
sources: Castelnovo, Moessner & Sondhi (2008). "Magnetic monopoles in spin ice". *Nature* 451, 42. [arXiv:0710.5515](https://arxiv.org/abs/0710.5515)

name: Skyrmions and cosmic textures
summary: Magnetic skyrmions and cosmological textures are both non-singular topological solitons of a sphere-valued order parameter classified by homotopy (pi_2 for 2D films, pi_3 for 3D cosmic textures); a collapsing texture was proposed to explain the CMB Cold Spot.
breaks: Skyrmions are static, DMI-stabilized and 2D; cosmic textures are 3D, unstable to collapse by Derrick's theorem and scale with the horizon. The Cold Spot texture interpretation is not established.
sources: Turok (1989). "Global texture as the origin of cosmic structure". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 63, 2625. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.63.2625](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.63.2625)
Cruz et al. (2007). "A Cosmic Microwave Background Feature Consistent with a Cosmic Texture". *Science* 318, 1612. [arXiv:0710.5737](https://arxiv.org/abs/0710.5737)

name: Dust aggregation: from colloids to planetesimals
summary: The first stage of planet formation is aggregation of micron dust grains by Brownian motion and differential drift into fractal aggregates, followed by compaction, bouncing and fragmentation: the cluster-cluster aggregation and contact mechanics studied in colloids and granular matter.
map: D=\frac{k_BT}{6\pi\eta a}\to t_s=\frac{\rho_sa}{\rho_gv_{th}}\ (\text{Epstein});\ N\propto R^{d_f},\ d_f\approx1.8\text{-}2
sources: Blum & Wurm (2008). "The Growth Mechanisms of Macroscopic Bodies in Protoplanetary Disks". *Annu. Rev. Astron. Astrophys.* 46, 21. [doi:10.1146/annurev.astro.46.060407.145152](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev.astro.46.060407.145152)

name: Rubble-pile asteroids as granular bodies
summary: Most km-sized asteroids (Itokawa, Ryugu, Bennu) are gravitationally bound granular aggregates whose shapes, spin limits, regolith segregation and response to spacecraft contact are governed by granular rheology, friction and weak cohesion.
sources: Walsh (2018). "Rubble Pile Asteroids". *Annu. Rev. Astron. Astrophys.* 56, 593. [doi:10.1146/annurev-astro-081817-052013](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-astro-081817-052013)

name: Amorphous ices and silicates in disks and dust
summary: Interstellar and protoplanetary grains are largely amorphous: vapour-deposited amorphous solid water and glassy silicates whose crystallization (annealing near the star) and glass-transition kinetics record thermal history and control volatile trapping at snow lines.

name: Kibble-Zurek defects: liquid crystals and the early universe
summary: Kibble's argument that causally disconnected regions choose independent vacua at a symmetry-breaking transition, leaving strings and monopoles whose overabundance inflation must dilute, was tested by quenching nematic liquid crystals and counting disclinations; Zurek's refinement gives defect density from the quench rate.
breaks: Nematic defects form in a dissipative, non-relativistic fluid with no gauge field and coarsen by friction; cosmic defects are relativistic, may be gauge strings, and evolve in an expanding spacetime.
sources: Kibble (1976). "Topology of cosmic domains and strings". *J. Phys. A* 9, 1387. [doi:10.1088/0305-4470/9/8/029](https://doi.org/10.1088/0305-4470/9/8/029)
Zurek (1985). "Cosmological experiments in superfluid helium?". *Nature* 317, 505. [doi:10.1038/317505a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/317505a0)
Chuang et al. (1991). "Cosmology in the Laboratory: Defect Dynamics in Liquid Crystals". *Science* 251, 1336. [doi:10.1126/science.251.4999.1336](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.251.4999.1336)

name: Nuclear pasta as a liquid crystal
summary: In the neutron-star mantle, competition between nuclear surface tension and long-range Coulomb repulsion produces rod, slab and bubble 'pasta' phases with the symmetries of columnar and smectic liquid crystals (and of block-copolymer microphases); their elasticity is described with liquid-crystal theory.
breaks: Pasta is ordered by nuclear plus Coulomb forces at ~1e14 g/cm^3 with no solvent or thermal softness; its elastic constants are MeV-scale and the phases sit in a degenerate electron sea.
sources: Pethick & Potekhin (1998). "Liquid crystals in the mantles of neutron stars". *Phys. Lett. B* 427, 7. [arXiv:astro-ph/9803154](https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/9803154)
Caplan & Horowitz (2017). "Colloquium: Astromaterial science and nuclear pasta". *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 89, 041002. [arXiv:1606.03646](https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.03646)

name: Superconducting detectors for the CMB: TES and MKIDs
summary: CMB experiments (BICEP/Keck, SPT, ACT, Simons Observatory, CMB-S4) use arrays of transition-edge-sensor bolometers biased on the steep R(T) of a superconducting transition, and kinetic-inductance detectors that sense photon pair breaking through the Cooper-pair kinetic inductance.
sources: Irwin (1995). "An application of electrothermal feedback for high resolution cryogenic particle detection". *Appl. Phys. Lett.* 66, 1998. [doi:10.1063/1.113674](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.113674)
Day et al. (2003). "A broadband superconducting detector suitable for use in large arrays". *Nature* 425, 817. [doi:10.1038/nature02037](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature02037)

name: Cosmic-string formation simulated in superfluid 3He
summary: Neutron-absorption hot spots in BCS-paired superfluid 3He re-cool through Tc and nucleate vortex tangles at the rate predicted by the Kibble-Zurek mechanism, a laboratory test of defect formation in early-universe phase transitions with a multicomponent order parameter.
breaks: 3He is a non-relativistic p-wave condensate whose vortices are global (no gauge field), whereas GUT strings are relativistic and typically local; the quench is spatially inhomogeneous, unlike a cosmological transition.
sources: Bäuerle et al. (1996). "Laboratory simulation of cosmic string formation in the early Universe using superfluid 3He". *Nature* 382, 332. [doi:10.1038/382332a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/382332a0)
Ruutu et al. (1996). "Vortex formation in neutron-irradiated superfluid 3He as an analogue of cosmic-string formation". *Nature* 382, 334. [doi:10.1038/382334a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/382334a0)

name: Superconducting phonon sensors and targets for dark matter
summary: Cryogenic dark-matter searches (SuperCDMS, CRESST) read athermal phonons from keV nuclear recoils with tungsten transition-edge sensors; superconductors themselves are proposed as targets for keV-mass dark matter because the gap 2Delta~meV sets an ultra-low threshold.
sources: Hochberg, Zhao & Zurek (2016). "Superconducting Detectors for Superlight Dark Matter". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 116, 011301. [arXiv:1504.07237](https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.07237)

name: Cosmic rays and pair breaking in superconducting devices
summary: Cosmic-ray muons and environmental gamma rays deposit energy in substrates as athermal phonons that break Cooper pairs, causing correlated quasiparticle bursts and error avalanches in superconducting qubits; this is the pair-breaking channel that cryogenic detectors use to see particles.
sources: McEwen et al. (2022). "Resolving catastrophic error bursts from cosmic rays in large arrays of superconducting qubits". *Nat. Phys.* 18, 107. [arXiv:2104.05219](https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.05219)
Vepsäläinen et al. (2020). "Impact of ionizing radiation on superconducting qubit coherence". *Nature* 584, 551. [arXiv:2001.09190](https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.09190)

name: Nucleon pairing and neutron-star superfluidity
summary: The BCS gap equation with nuclear instead of phonon attraction gives 1S0 neutron superfluidity in the inner crust and 3P2 neutron and 1S0 proton pairing in the core; pair-breaking-formation neutrino emission just below Tc explains the rapid cooling of the Cas A neutron star.
sources: Baym, Pethick & Pines (1969). "Superfluidity in Neutron Stars". *Nature* 224, 673. [doi:10.1038/224673a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/224673a0)

Page et al. (2011). "Rapid Cooling of the Neutron Star in Cassiopeia A Triggered by Neutron Superfluidity in Dense Matter". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 106, 081101. [arXiv:1011.6142](https://arxiv.org/abs/1011.6142)

name: Vortex pinning and creep: flux lines vs pulsar glitches
summary: Pulsar glitches are modelled as catastrophic unpinning of quantized neutron-superfluid vortices from the crust lattice, the physics of Abrikosov flux-line pinning and Anderson-Kim thermally activated flux creep in type-II superconductors; post-glitch relaxation is vortex creep.
map: \oint\mathbf v_s\cdot d\mathbf l=h/2m_n\ (\text{neutron vortex})\leftrightarrow\Phi_0=h/2e\ (\text{flux line});\ \text{Magnus}\leftrightarrow\text{Lorentz force}
breaks: Neutron vortices are neutral and feel Magnus rather than Lorentz forces; pinning sites are nuclei of a Coulomb lattice, not material defects, and entrainment couples the superfluid to the crust.
sources: Anderson & Itoh (1975). "Pulsar glitches and restlessness as a hard superfluidity phenomenon". *Nature* 256, 25. [doi:10.1038/256025a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/256025a0)
Andersson et al. (2012). "Pulsar Glitches: The Crust is not Enough". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 109, 241103. [arXiv:1207.0633](https://arxiv.org/abs/1207.0633)

name: Metallic hydrogen in giant planets
summary: Metallic hydrogen, predicted by Wigner and Huntington and proposed by Ashcroft as a high-Tc phonon superconductor (the idea behind hydride superconductors), makes up most of Jupiter's and Saturn's interiors, where its conductivity powers their dynamos; shock and static compression of the insulator-metal transition serve both fields.
sources: Wigner & Huntington (1935). "On the Possibility of a Metallic Modification of Hydrogen". *J. Chem. Phys.* 3, 764. [doi:10.1063/1.1749590](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.1749590)
Ashcroft (1968). "Metallic Hydrogen: A High-Temperature Superconductor?". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 21, 1748. [doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.21.1748](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.21.1748)
Celliers et al. (2018). "Insulator-metal transition in dense fluid deuterium". *Science* 361, 677. [doi:10.1126/science.aat0970](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aat0970)

name: SQUID multiplexed readout of detector arrays
summary: Kilo- to hundred-thousand-pixel TES arrays for CMB polarimetry are read out with SQUID amplifiers in time-division or microwave (rf-SQUID resonator) multiplexing, exploiting the flux-periodic Josephson response and its low noise.

name: Josephson parametric amplifiers in axion haloscopes
summary: Axion haloscopes (ADMX, HAYSTAC) detect axion-to-photon conversion in a microwave cavity with Josephson parametric amplifiers operating near the standard quantum limit, and HAYSTAC's squeezed-vacuum readout beats it.
sources: Du et al. (2018). "Search for Invisible Axion Dark Matter with the Axion Dark Matter Experiment". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 120, 151301. [arXiv:1804.05750](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.05750)
Backes et al. (2021). "A quantum enhanced search for dark matter axions". *Nature* 590, 238. [arXiv:2008.01853](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.01853)

name: Axion quasiparticles in magnetic topological insulators
summary: Magnetic topological insulators host a dynamical axion field theta(t) coupling as theta E.B; its quasiparticle (a longitudinal antiferromagnetic magnon mode) is proposed as a tunable meV-scale medium that converts axion dark matter into THz photons.
map: \mathcal L_\theta=\frac{\theta e^2}{2\pi h}\mathbf E\cdot\mathbf B\leftrightarrow\mathcal L_a=g_{a\gamma\gamma}\,a\,\mathbf E\cdot\mathbf B
breaks: The solid-state axion is an emergent collective mode with a material-set mass, not the QCD axion; only the electrodynamic coupling form is shared, and no candidate material is yet confirmed.
sources: Marsh et al. (2019). "Proposal to Detect Dark Matter using Axionic Topological Antiferromagnets". *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 123, 121601. [arXiv:1807.08810](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.08810)

name: Dirac materials as light dark-matter targets
summary: 3D Dirac and Weyl semimetals with meV-scale gaps and weak in-medium screening have been proposed as targets for sub-MeV dark matter scattering or absorption on electrons, with directional sensitivity from anisotropic Dirac cones.
map: H_W=\hbar v_F\boldsymbol\sigma\cdot\mathbf k,\ E_g\to\text{meV};\ v_F\ll c\ \text{matches DM kinematics}
sources: Hochberg et al. (2018). "Detection of sub-MeV dark matter with three-dimensional Dirac materials". *Phys. Rev. D* 97, 015004. [arXiv:1708.08929](https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.08929)

name: CMB tests inflationary predictions
summary: Near scale-invariant adiabatic Gaussian fluctuations, the spectral tilt and limits on tensor modes from B-mode polarization constrain inflationary models.

name: Acoustic oscillations as standard ruler
summary: The same sound horizon at the drag epoch imprinted in the CMB peaks appears as the BAO feature in galaxy clustering, giving a standard ruler across redshift.

name: CMB acoustic peaks require non-baryonic matter
summary: Relative heights of the acoustic peaks fix the baryon and total matter densities; the third peak demands collisionless dark matter that decoupled potentials from the photon-baryon fluid.

name: Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect
summary: Inverse-Compton scattering of CMB photons by hot intracluster electrons distorts the CMB spectrum, yielding cluster catalogs and pressure profiles.

name: Reionization imprinted on the CMB
summary: Thomson scattering from free electrons after reionization gives the optical depth tau and large-angle E-mode polarization bump, plus kinetic SZ, constraining when first galaxies ionized the universe.

name: BAO and DESI dark-energy constraints
summary: BAO distances combined with supernovae and CMB constrain the dark-energy equation of state; DESI hints at evolving w.

name: Supernova systematics in the dark-energy era
summary: Progenitor, host-galaxy and dust effects on Type Ia luminosities limit precision on the dark-energy equation of state, relevant to DESI and Rubin-era samples.

name: Type Ia supernovae as standard candles
summary: Type Ia light curves, standardised by width-luminosity corrections, give luminosity distances that revealed cosmic acceleration; stellar explosion physics sets the systematics of the dark-energy inference.

name: Dark matter in the Friedmann budget
summary: Evidence from CMB, BBN and structure growth fixes the cold dark matter density parameter in the Friedmann equation that sets expansion history.

name: Time-delay cosmography and cosmic shear
summary: Strong-lens time delays give H0 independent of the distance ladder, while weak-lensing shear measures S8, the other tension.

name: Lensing maps dark matter
summary: Lensing responds to total mass irrespective of luminosity, so strong and weak lensing give direct mass maps and halo profiles, as in the Bullet Cluster and subhalo searches.

name: Lensing probes dark subhalos
summary: Flux-ratio anomalies and gravitational imaging of strong lenses detect low-mass subhalos, constraining warm, fuzzy and self-interacting dark matter on sub-galactic scales.

name: Microlensing finds planets
summary: Gravitational microlensing, developed for MACHO searches, detects cold and free-floating planets beyond the reach of transits and radial velocity.

name: Distance ladder and Hubble tension
summary: Cepheid and TRGB calibrated Type Ia supernovae set the local H0 that disagrees with CMB inference; stellar physics systematics are central to the dispute.

name: Hierarchical growth from primordial perturbations
summary: Gravitational growth of primordial density perturbations builds halos, filaments and then galaxies; large-scale structure statistics supply the initial conditions for galaxy formation.

name: Galaxy bias links halos to the matter field
summary: Galaxy surveys trace the cosmic web only through galaxy formation physics; halo occupation and bias connect observed clustering to the underlying matter power spectrum.

name: Dark halos host galaxies
summary: Galaxies form within dark-matter halos, whose potentials set rotation curves, scaling relations and merger histories.

name: Cluster problem for MOND
summary: MOND fits rotation curves but needs extra unseen mass in clusters, and the Bullet Cluster lensing offset challenges it.
breaks: Fails at cluster scales without additional dark components such as sterile neutrinos.

name: Galaxy scaling relations and MOND
summary: Baryonic Tully-Fisher and the radial acceleration relation are tight galaxy scaling laws that MOND predicts directly, whereas CDM must reproduce them through feedback.

name: Cluster dynamics, gas and lensing mass
summary: Zwicky's virial argument, X-ray hydrostatic gas masses and lensing all show clusters dominated by dark matter, and the Bullet Cluster separates the mass from the baryons.

name: Clusters as dark-matter laboratories
summary: Cluster mass budgets from X-ray hydrostatic equilibrium, SZ, lensing and galaxy velocities give dark-matter fractions and collisional constraints.

name: Galactic dynamics and the local halo
summary: Milky Way rotation curve, Gaia stellar streams and escape velocity measure the halo mass and local density, key inputs to direct-detection rates.

name: Baryonic feedback vs dark-matter physics
summary: Cusp-core, missing satellites and too-big-to-fail can be solved either by new dark-matter physics or by supernova feedback and reionization suppressing dwarf galaxy formation; the two are degenerate.

name: Dwarf galaxy tests of CDM
summary: Dwarf galaxy scaling relations and simulations are the testing ground for CDM versus alternatives, with baryonic physics the key systematic.

name: Cosmic-ray backgrounds for dark-matter signals
summary: Antiprotons, positrons and gamma rays from dark-matter annihilation must be separated from astrophysical cosmic-ray production and propagation, as in the positron excess and antiproton debates.

name: AGN as neutrino sources
summary: Blazars such as TXS 0506+056 and Seyferts like NGC 1068 are identified IceCube sources; hadronic acceleration in jets and coronae produces neutrinos with gamma rays.

name: Accretion disk theory shared
summary: Shakura-Sunyaev alpha disks and MRI-driven turbulence describe both AGN accretion and protoplanetary disks.
breaks: Disk temperature, ionization and radiation pressure regimes differ by many orders of magnitude, so MRI activity and dead zones apply differently.

name: Stellar populations as galactic archaeology
summary: Ages, abundances and kinematics of stellar populations, with Gaia, reconstruct the Milky Way's assembly history and star-formation history.

name: Supernova remnants accelerate cosmic rays
summary: Diffusive shock acceleration at supernova remnant shocks is the standard origin of Galactic cosmic rays up to the knee.

name: Magnetars as FRB engines
summary: The Galactic magnetar SGR 1935+2154 emitted an FRB-like burst, tying FRBs to highly magnetised neutron stars.

name: Short GRBs from neutron-star mergers
summary: GW170817 with GRB 170817A and the kilonova established compact mergers as short-GRB progenitors, with off-axis jet physics.

name: Long GRBs and collapsars
summary: Long GRBs accompany broad-lined Type Ic supernovae from collapsing massive stars, linking relativistic jets to core-collapse explosions.

name: Gravitational waves from compact binaries
summary: Neutron-star and black-hole mergers are the gravitational-wave sources; kilonovae probe r-process nucleosynthesis and dense-matter equation of state.

name: Solar neutrinos and neutrino astronomy
summary: Solar neutrino detection, resolving the solar neutrino problem via oscillations, established the techniques and flavor physics later used in astrophysical neutrino telescopes.

name: Radiative transfer in atmospheres
summary: Exoplanet atmosphere retrievals use radiative transfer and opacities developed for stellar atmospheres, and stellar activity and limb darkening contaminate transmission spectra.

name: Disks around young stars and accretion
summary: Viscous accretion disks govern protoplanetary evolution and mass transfer in binaries, sharing alpha-disk transport and angular-momentum redistribution.
breaks: Protoplanetary disks are cool, dusty and partly neutral, so non-ideal MHD and dust dynamics differ from ionized binary disks.

name: Degeneracy pressure sets remnant masses
summary: Stellar evolution ends in white dwarfs, neutron stars or black holes, and degeneracy pressure support yields the Chandrasekhar and TOV mass limits.

name: Primordial plasma and Thomson scattering
summary: Before recombination the universe was a tightly coupled photon–baryon plasma, whose acoustic oscillations imprint the CMB peaks. Thomson scattering off free electrons sets the optical depth, and reionization polarizes the CMB.

name: BAO as sound waves in the primordial plasma
summary: Baryon acoustic oscillations are ion-acoustic-like pressure waves in the coupled photon–baryon fluid. The sound horizon is a standard ruler, and Jeans instability parallels plasma streaming and gravitational instabilities.
breaks: Gravity and radiation drag replace electrostatic restoring forces, and there is no Debye-scale dispersion.

name: Magnetically driven AGN jets
summary: Relativistic AGN jets are launched and collimated by magnetic fields threading a black hole or disk, as in Blandford–Znajek and Blandford–Payne. These are force-free and relativistic MHD flows.

name: Reconnection in jets and coronae
summary: Relativistic reconnection and plasmoid chains are invoked for particle acceleration and fast blazar flares, and for heating accretion-disk coronae.

name: Turbulence and magnetic fields in clusters
summary: Cluster mergers and AGN drive turbulence that amplifies magnetic fields by a small-scale turbulent dynamo. Radio halos arise from turbulent reacceleration of relativistic electrons.

name: Intracluster medium as a weakly collisional plasma
summary: The hot, magnetised intracluster medium has long mean free paths, so pressure anisotropy, firehose and mirror instabilities, and suppressed Spitzer conduction require kinetic treatment. Plasma microinstabilities regulate viscosity and heat transport.

name: Reionization and the intergalactic plasma
summary: Reionization turned the neutral intergalactic medium into a tenuous, ionized plasma. Its free-electron column sets the CMB optical depth and the FRB dispersion measure.

name: Galactic dynamo and seed fields
summary: Galactic magnetic fields of microgauss strength are explained by mean-field αΩ dynamos acting on weak seed fields. Fluctuation dynamos amplify fields in early galaxies, and the seed origin remains open.

name: Astroparticle sources are astrophysical plasma shocks
summary: High-energy astrophysical sources accelerate particles in collisionless shocks and magnetised outflows, so plasma shock physics underlies cosmic-ray, GRB and neutrino source modelling.

name: Plasma wakefield acceleration and astrophysical acceleration
summary: Wakefield acceleration and cosmic-ray acceleration both push charged particles to high energy in collective plasma fields, and wakefield-type mechanisms are proposed for UHECR. Wakefields are coherent and laminar while Fermi processes are stochastic.
breaks: Wakefields give deterministic gradients in a driven wave, while Fermi acceleration is statistical scattering across a shock.

name: Alfvén waves scatter cosmic rays
summary: Cosmic rays stream along field lines and resonantly excite Alfvén waves, which scatter them and set the diffusion coefficient. Self-generated waves confine Galactic cosmic rays and feed back in shock precursors.

name: Turbulent scattering and cosmic-ray transport
summary: Cosmic-ray diffusion in the Galaxy is set by scattering off MHD turbulence. Goldreich–Sridhar anisotropy makes resonant scattering by Alfvénic modes inefficient, so compressive modes and cascade properties matter.

name: Cosmic rays and heliospheric particle physics
summary: Galactic cosmic rays propagate through the turbulent magnetised solar wind and heliosphere, where modulation, diffusion and scattering are plasma processes. The same transport theory applies in the Galaxy.

name: Diffusive shock acceleration of cosmic rays
summary: First-order Fermi acceleration at collisionless shocks yields a power-law spectrum p^-(3r/(r-1)) with index near 2 for strong shocks, and explains the cosmic-ray spectrum from supernova remnants. Magnetic-field amplification enables acceleration toward the knee.

name: FRB emission as coherent plasma processes
summary: FRB models invoke coherent emission from plasma instabilities, maser-like shock emission and magnetospheric reconnection. Propagation through plasma produces dispersion, scattering and Faraday rotation, which make FRBs probes of intergalactic baryons.

name: GRB afterglows from relativistic collisionless shocks
summary: GRB afterglow synchrotron emission arises from relativistic collisionless shocks, where Weibel-type instabilities generate magnetic fields and accelerate electrons. PIC simulations of these shocks inform the microphysical parameters ε_B and ε_e.

name: Planetary interiors at megabar pressures
summary: Giant-planet interiors contain hydrogen, helium and water at megabar pressures, where laser shock experiments measure the equation of state, metallization and demixing. Results feed interior and evolution models.

name: Magnetised accretion disks and the MRI
summary: Angular momentum transport in ionised protoplanetary disks is driven by the magnetorotational instability. Nonideal MHD effects (Ohmic, Hall, ambipolar) and disk winds set accretion and dead zones.

name: Disk MRI from ideal-MHD Alfvén dynamics
summary: The MRI is an ideal-MHD instability in which a weak field acts like a spring tying fluid elements in differential rotation, an Alfvén-wave tension effect. It drives disk turbulence and angular momentum transport.

name: Stellar interiors and atmospheres are plasmas
summary: Stars are self-gravitating plasmas. Their equation of state, opacity, transport, convection, magnetism and winds draw on plasma physics, and fusion burning links to laboratory fusion.

name: Dense matter equations of state in the lab
summary: Laser-driven shocks and X-ray Thomson scattering probe warm dense matter relevant to white-dwarf and giant-planet interiors. Laboratory equations of state calibrate dense-plasma models for compact objects.

name: Pulsar wind nebulae and relativistic shocks
summary: Pulsar winds terminate in relativistic shocks that accelerate pairs and power synchrotron nebulae such as the Crab. These are testbeds for relativistic shock acceleration and magnetic reconnection in striped winds.

name: Stellar nucleosynthesis and fusion burning
summary: Stars burn by thermonuclear fusion with Gamow-peak reaction rates, and fusion devices target the same reactions. Laboratory D-T burning plasmas are self-heated by alphas, like stellar cores.
breaks: Stars confine by gravity at about 10^7 K and long timescales, while devices use magnetic fields at 10^8 K and lack gravitational stability.

name: Rayleigh–Taylor mixing in supernovae and ICF
summary: Hydrodynamic instabilities at accelerating interfaces occur in core-collapse explosions and in ICF capsule implosions. Scaled laser experiments reproduce supernova mixing, and the shared physics is Rayleigh–Taylor and Richtmyer–Meshkov growth.
breaks: ICF has ablation stabilization and sharp interfaces, while supernovae involve gravity, neutrinos and nuclear burning.

name: Supernova remnant shocks
summary: Supernova remnants are the canonical sites of collisionless shocks, with magnetic-field amplification, thin X-ray rims and gamma-ray emission. They are the leading candidate sources of Galactic cosmic rays.

name: Solar magnetism as MHD
summary: Sunspots, flux emergence, flares and coronal structure are MHD phenomena. Frozen-in flux, reconnection and Alfvén waves describe the Sun's magnetic activity.

name: The solar dynamo and the solar cycle
summary: The 11-year solar cycle is produced by a dynamo in which differential rotation (the Ω-effect) and helical convection (the α-effect) regenerate field. Helioseismology constrains the rotation profile that feeds mean-field models.

name: Solar flares as reconnection
summary: Solar flares and CMEs release stored magnetic energy by reconnection, per the standard CSHKP model. The Sweet–Parker rate is too slow, which motivated plasmoid and collisionless reconnection.

name: Sun to heliosphere
summary: The Sun drives the solar wind, coronal mass ejections and space weather. Helioseismology and coronal physics set the boundary conditions for heliospheric plasma models.
